atomic_functions.name: payout_cell_edit

Cancel closes the editor with zero writes. Matured positions keep a non-editable Matured chip — never an editable cell (FR-67).

atomic_functions.name: month_columns_elapsed_current
atomic_functions.purpose: Compute the Payouts grid month columns as elapsed months plus the current month ONLY, ordered newest month first at the left and oldest visible month at the right (D42, FR-68): the tenure window (tenure_month_map / list_months_through_current pattern) is filtered to months <= the current month key and then reversed for newest-left order. atomic_functions.name: sort_key_appwide
atomic_functions.purpose: Own the ONE app-wide ordering function the owner LOCKED as D43: a single shared sort key fed by HEALTH_ORDER = {Danger: 0, On-going: 1, Matured: 2, Invalid: 3} — Danger first, On-going next, Matured (Completed) last, and Invalid (incomplete or unreadable rows) last of all — applied to EVERY list surface: Dashboard (AF-79), My Holdings, Payouts (the AF-68 sort becomes one caller of this function), exports, print and alerts. The key is (HEALTH_ORDER[status], company lowercased, row id); an unknown health value raises the named ERR-payout-sort error rather than silently falling back, matching the engine pattern. The D43 status taxonomy is codified here: Danger = immediate attention required (missed payment, overdue, missing data); On-going = active and progressing normally, nothing needs attention; Matured/Completed = successfully finished, no further action. Danger assignment stays AUTOMATIC by business rule — a passed credit day with no payment entered by the due date makes the position Danger the same day (due on the 1st, not entered by the 1st, is Danger on the 1st) — with no manual status field anywhere. This function is the ONLY place the ordering lives; no screen reimplements it (D43 LOCKED).

the status value produced by the day-wise engine (AF-67) — read, never written here

named ERR-payout-sort error on an unknown health value — no silent fallback
the one shared ordering every list surface imports
triggers: any list render: dashboard, holdings, payouts, exports, print, alerts
any health re-derivation that changes a row's status before a re-sort

atomic_functions.name: returns_history_aggregate
atomic_functions.purpose: Aggregate the Returns history Dashboard tab (D42, FR-73): a month table with columns Month, Interest received, Positions paid · pending (of active positions) and Cumulative received, newest month first, the current month highlighted, future months never shown. Per month: Interest received = the total amount credited in that month (SUM of paid payment_ledger rows for that month); Positions paid · pending = count of ACTIVE positions paid for that month · count of active positions still awaiting it; Cumulative received = the running total of all interest from the first payout through that month, its latest row equal to the Received KPI card. The SQL sketch groups payment_ledger by month and orders month DESC, restricted to months <= the current month key (elapsed + current only, F-231 discipline) and to active positions for the paid/pending counts.

outputs: month rows newest first: month label, interest received total, paid · pending counts of active positions, cumulative running total
current-month row flagged for highlight; no future month rows

triggers: Dashboard Returns history tab render
payment save re-derivation (AF-75) invalidating the cached aggregate

atomic_functions.name: credit_day_check_migration
atomic_functions.purpose: Migrate the bonds.credit_day storage constraint from CHECK (credit_day >= 1 AND credit_day <= 28) to 1..31 (D41 owner rule carried into the D42 wave, FR-74 credit-day field enabler, SRS v6 implementation caution (a)): SQLite cannot ALTER a CHECK constraint, so the migration performs a one-time table rebuild — create bonds_new with the widened CHECK, copy every row, drop the old table, rename — preserving all rows and ids. The rebuild runs inside the boot schema-ensure path before any insert path (candidate add, move to portfolio, add position) writes a credit day, so an insert of 29..31 never fails at the storage layer while app-level validation already accepts 1..31 (FR-54). The migration is idempotent: a stored marker in alert_prefs plus a PRAGMA table_info guard makes a second boot a no-op.
